headline: UPDATE + CLAIM-BUST to the Hormuz ship-on-fire thread -- UKMTO
dek: [VERIFIED FACT - identification; ATTRIBUTED REPORT - incident details] UKMTO says regional authorities identified the vessel that sustained fire off the Omani coast as a dhow involved in a maritime security incident; a large fire onboard caused it to list and sink, and its crew has been evacuated.…
sources: UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) statement via Al Jazeera liveblog
fault_line: Tanker war or fog of war? Every fire at Hormuz gets claimed as a tanker strike -- this one was a dhow. How much of the shipping-war picture is real, and how much is claim?

sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT - identification; ATTRIBUTED REPORT - incident details] UKMTO says regional authorities identified the vessel that sustained fire off the Omani coast as a dhow involved in a maritime security incident; a large fire onboard caused it to list and sink, and its crew has been evacuated. The incident occurred 9 nautical miles (about 17 km) north of Khasab, Oman. This RESOLVES the previously unlinked UKMTO ship-on-fire report: it was a dhow, NOT one of the tankers in Iran's mine claims (1900-01 fourth tanker; 1300-01 southern-route three). Do not link the dhow to any tanker claim.
sections.what_verified: UKMTO (T1, OFFICIAL-PD) is itself the primary source for this incident report; the record states so explicitly per the single-family rule.
sections.what_disputed: No claimant has linked the dhow to the tanker mine claims; Iran's army/IRGC statements describe tankers, not dhows. Cause of the dhow fire (attack vs accident) is NOT stated by UKMTO in the retrieved entry -- do not call it an attack.
sections.why_matters: The 'ship on fire' at Hormuz was NOT a tanker: UKMTO identifies a dhow, crew evacuated, vessel sank -- a claim-busting correction inside the shipping-war thread
sections.context: Background: UPDATE + CLAIM-BUST to the Hormuz ship-on-fire thread -- UKMTO: the vessel on fire 9 nm north of Khasab was a DHOW, crew evacuated, vessel listed and sank -- not a tanker

totw_analysis: Our read: The 'ship on fire' at Hormuz was NOT a tanker: UKMTO identifies a dhow, crew evacuated, vessel sank -- a claim-busting correction inside the shipping-war thread The fault line our audience is arguing over: Tanker war or fog of war? Every fire at Hormuz gets claimed as a tanker strike -- this one was a dhow. How much of the shipping-war picture is real, and how much is claim?
